bodyText:
Contributing guidelines

 I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)
mini.ai
Question
vimtex has some commands like  <plug>(vimtex-ae) (ie around environment). Is it possible to define custom textobjects for mini.ai using vimtex's textobjects?
Thanks

comment_data.body:
Custom textobjects in 'mini.ai' need to follow [textobject specification](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a84b7e555fe382c1859e6ca46b4983c822a1f77f/doc/mini-ai.txt#L252). Which essentially means:
- Use nested/composed Lua patterns to define the rule for matching regions inside string. This probably doesn't fit in the use case.
- Allow function as part of nested/composed Lua pattern. Same resolution as the previous one.
- Use function as textobject specification. It can return nested/composed pattern (no good use here), single region to be used as is, or array of regions to "smartly" select from based on `[count]` / `search_method` / etc. If there is a way to programmatically get the information from vimtex plugin, then it would be possible.

I am not aware of any way to extract necessary region information just from `<Plug>` mapping, as those are specifically designed to be used inside mapping. I think even if possible, it would be *very* hacky.

Other than that, I'd like to point out that there is no need to define custom textobject in 'mini.ai' in order to use textobjects from vimtex. If 'mini.ai' doesn't find its own specification for some textobject id, it will fall back to whichever textobject there is without 'mini.ai'. For example, built-in `aw` / `iw` still work even though there is no built-in or custom `w` textobject in 'mini.ai'. To force the fallback (like in case of built-in character identifiers or punctuation/digits/whitespace), [set custom textobject to `false`](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/a84b7e555fe382c1859e6ca46b4983c822a1f77f/doc/mini-ai.txt#L483-L484).

So just using `ae` textobject via `<Plug>...` mapping should keep working. It will not work with "next" / "last" variants, though, for which there needs to be custom textobject (which requires some programmatic interface from vimtex outside of just `<Plug>` mappings).
